findings.summary: `var pingTimer;` is declared but the `setInterval(...)` call on the next line never assigns its return value to it (`pingTimer=setInterval(...)` was needed). `clearInterval(pingTimer)` in `onclose` therefore calls `clearInterval(undefined)`, a no-op — the actual interval ID is never captured and never cleared. This is the exact failure mode the brief explicitly called out to prevent: every reconnect (`ws.onclose` -> `setTimeout(connect,3000)`) spins up a brand-new `connect()` closure with its own permanently-running `setInterval`, and none of the previous ones are ever torn down, so repeated drops/reconnects leave an ever-growing number of ping loops running concurrently, each firing `ws.send('ping')` on its own (now-closed or stale) `ws` reference every 15s indefinitely.

findings.summary: The new test only checks that the literal substring `clearInterval(pingTimer)` appears in the emitted script text; it never executes the script to verify the timer is actually captured and cleared. Because of this, the test passes identically whether or not `pingTimer=setInterval(...)` is written — it cannot distinguish the broken code (assignment missing, confirmed present at HEAD) from a correct fix, so it gives false confidence that the reconnect-leak requirement is met.
